Subject: Request: temporary lane swap for Q3 burst (Evergreen Health)

Hi Laura,

Hope you’re well. We’ve had an unexpected acceleration in our model training timelines — a partner integration pushed a portion of our inference load to Q3 earlier than planned. We have a reserved Dedicated pool with Redwood under DEAL-1529, but we don’t have the burst lanes we expected available in the first week of July.

Would Redwood consider a temporary lane swap or short-term reallocation so we can front-load ~480 GPU-hours during July 1–3? We’re open to a targeted preemption policy, and we can discuss one-time credits in exchange. I’ve attached a short schedule and the commitment summary.

We’re trying to avoid model retraining delays that would cascade customer launch timelines. Please let me know what information you need from our side; happy to jump on a call today.

Thanks,
Carolina Ruiz
Head of ML Ops, Evergreen Health

Laura — quick commercial note. DEAL-1529 contains reserved capacity with a limited burst allowance and a credit schedule only for sustained overage, not one-off swaps. We can do a one-off reallocation, but Finance and Legal need to sign off on the commercial trade-offs (credits vs. replaced burst windows).

Options I see:
1) One-off lane swap for up to 72 hours with a 15% revenue credit applied to July usage (fast to approve, but needs Finance sign-off).
2) Formal amendment to the SOW to expand July burst by X GPUs — longer lead time, requires legal and procurement.
3) Preferential temporary preemption where Evergreen takes preemptible lanes at lower rate; lower commercial impact but higher operational risk for them.

If Laura wants to approve a tactical swap, I can open a Finance approval ticket and draft the one-off credit memo. Otherwise we’ll need legal to start an amendment.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary lane swap for Q3 burst (Evergreen Health)

Thanks for the ping. Operational summary — current Dedicated pool utilization for the US-east cluster: committed reserved lanes at ~84% baseline, with scheduled bursts from NebulaAI and HelioLabs the week prior to your requested window. That said, there are three technical approaches we can safely consider (ordered by operational risk):

A) Controlled lane-swap (recommended): carve 12 gpus from lower-priority burst reservations (pre-agreed partner lanes) and reassign to Evergreen for 72 hours. We’d enforce KV-cache isolation and throttle token concurrency to mitigate tail-latency impact. Estimated cost to Evergreen: ~480 GPU-hours; risk to others: minimal if we throttle.

B) Preemptible burst allocation: give Evergreen preemptible lanes with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant. Lower SLA guarantee, lower cost. Useful if Evergreen accepts throughput degradation under contention.

C) Shift NebulaAI burst window by 48 hours via an accommodation (requires partner consent) — highest coordination cost but no net preemption.

Operational caveats: we need 12 hours to stage the routing and test fallback policies, and a rollback plan. Also, if we go with A, we must document a hard preemption policy in the console and notify affected customers.

I recommend approving the controlled lane-swap (A) with a documented 72-hour timebox and a small credit (Ben’s suggestion). If approved, I’ll coordinate runbook updates and the rollout with infra on-call.

—Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: CAP-997-Runbook-diff.txt
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-01T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary lane swap for Q3 commitments — decision and next steps

Carolina — thank you for the fast turnaround. We will approve a controlled lane-swap (option A) for a 72-hour window: July 1 00:00 UTC → July 4 00:00 UTC, providing ~480 GPU-hours.

Commercials: Ben will prepare a one-time 15% usage credit for the July burst and submit for Finance sign-off this afternoon. Legal will be notified but we will not pursue a formal amendment given the one-off nature.

Operational: Karthik will schedule the staging/test window within the next 12 hours and publish the rollback/runbook. We will:
- Enforce preemption controls and token throttles.
- Notify NebulaAI of a 12-hour staging window and offer to shift their schedule if they choose (option C) — Ben, please coordinate that ask.
- Create a console alert for the lane-swap and tag the affected capacity slice.

Carolina: can you confirm the expected daily peak throughput for July 1–3 and whether Evergreen accepts the preemption policy (we will provide a fallback model variant if needed)? Once Ben confirms the credit path, we’ll publish the official schedule and send kickoff notes.

Thanks — will follow up with meeting notes and runbook links.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
